note: Test questions about karpathy/minGPT, written by the examiner (me) after reading the repo. Used by verify.py's QA carry test: closed-book (skill files only) vs open-book (whole repo). This is the miniature of the paper's A.2.2 recovery experiment: does the distilled skill carry the operational knowledge, or merely point back at the source?

questions.question: What are the three library files of minGPT and what does each contain?
questions.gold_answer: mingpt/model.py contains the actual Transformer model definition, mingpt/bpe.py contains a Byte Pair Encoder translating between text and sequences of integers, mingpt/trainer.py is GPT-independent PyTorch boilerplate that trains the model

questions.question: How do you install minGPT if you want to import mingpt into your project?
questions.gold_answer: git clone https://github.com/karpathy/minGPT.git, cd minGPT, pip install -e .

questions.question: Which class defines the GPT model and in which module?
questions.gold_answer: The GPT class (an nn.Module) in mingpt/model.py, with GPT.get_default_config for its configuration

questions.question: How do you load pretrained GPT-2 weights into minGPT?
questions.gold_answer: Call the classmethod GPT.from_pretrained(model_type) with model_type gpt2, gpt2-medium, gpt2-large or gpt2-xl; it downloads and loads the OpenAI GPT-2 checkpoint weights

questions.question: What does the Trainer class require at construction?
questions.gold_answer: Trainer(config, model, train_dataset): a TrainerConfig from Trainer.get_default_config, the model, and a training dataset

questions.question: What demo projects ship in the minGPT repository?
questions.gold_answer: projects/adder trains a GPT from scratch to add numbers, projects/chargpt trains a character-level language model on an input text file, demo.ipynb is a minimal GPT and Trainer usage on a sorting example, generate.ipynb loads a pretrained GPT2 and generates text

questions.question: Which utility function sets the random seed?
questions.gold_answer: set_seed(seed) in mingpt/utils.py, alongside setup_logging(config) and the CfgNode configuration class

questions.question: What is the signature of the generation method?
questions.gold_answer: GPT.generate(idx, max_new_tokens, temperature=1.0, do_sample=False, top_k=None) generates new tokens conditioned on the index sequence idx

questions.question: How is configuration handled in minGPT?
questions.gold_answer: CfgNode, a lightweight configuration class inspired by yacs in mingpt/utils.py, with merge_from_dict and merge_from_args to override defaults from command line arguments

questions.question: What is the maintenance status of the repository?
questions.gold_answer: Semi-archived state as of January 2023; for more recent developments use the rewrite nanoGPT
